newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal watchdog warns intermediaries on EDP sale.
newsitem.headline: Portugal watchdog warns intermediaries on EDP sale.

text.p: Portugal's financial watchdog has warned banks and brokers against encouraging clients to register for more shares in the coming privatisation of state electricity firm EDP than they really intend to buy.

The Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) said in a letter sent to banks and brokers that it was aware of cases in which intermediaries had encouraged clients to take loans to buy the stock or give them powers to subscribe on their behalf for the shares which look like being heavily over-booked.
"The CMVM believes that financial intermediaries should abstain from inducing clients to declare their intention to buy more stocks than they will eventually buy," it said.
Such activities damaged the transparency of the pre-registration period for the privatisation which was aimed at giving the seller a feel for the extent of demand, it said.
"They put at risk the credibility of the financial market and lead to a conflict of interest between intermediary and client," it said in the letter.
The pre-registration phase for the privatisation lasts until June 6. The bourse session to fix the price and the allocation of shares has been set for June 16.
